_status: Module 4, Lesson 4.2 'Shadow IT: the tool nobody approved', 'The approved-tools route' and 'What IT can add' (learner guide of 21 October 2026), including RA 10173 Secs 14 and 21(a). Fictional office and site; .example names are reserved for documentation.
title: Where does the masterlist go?

tracks.label: Shadow IT: the tool nobody approved

steps.title: Two masterlists, one deadline
steps.text: A colleague needs to merge two beneficiary masterlists by noon. A free online PDF converter would take one minute.

ask.q: Nothing leaks, and the file is deleted afterwards. Is there still a problem?
options: Yes: the office stays responsible, with no controls, no record and no way back
ask.why: Why it matters even when nothing leaks: the office stays responsible (RA 10173, Secs 14 and 21(a)); there are no controls and no record; and once uploaded, the data cannot be recalled.

steps.title: The upload: out of the office's control
steps.text: The masterlists leave for a site that has no agreement with the RSSO. The office cannot see who opens the file, where it is stored, or whether it can be deleted.

steps.title: No way back
steps.text: Whatever the site does next is out of reach. A personal information controller remains responsible for personal data it hands to another party (RA 10173, Sections 14 and 21(a)), and a free website has no agreement with the RSSO.

verdict.text: Shadow IT puts office data where nobody controls it.

tracks.label: Approved tools only
tracks.desk: Use approved tools only; ask before you upload. Report odd pop-ups and downloads.
tracks.it: An approved-tools list with a fast approval route; web filtering and data leakage prevention; security terms in every supplier contract.

steps.title: What IT can add: data leakage prevention
steps.text: Data leakage prevention warns or blocks when sensitive data leaves by email, upload or USB (ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A 8.12). Web filtering blocks known malicious and look-alike sites (8.23).

steps.title: The approved-tools route
steps.text: Ask first: is there an approved tool already? If not, request it; IT checks security and the DPO checks privacy; agree terms in writing if a vendor processes personal data; list it. **A fast route is itself a control:** people take workarounds when the official way is slow.

head: Step
The approved-tools route
rows: Is there an approved tool for this already?
If not, tell IT what you need to do and what data is involved
IT checks security; the DPO checks privacy, with a privacy impact assessment where personal data is involved
If the vendor will process personal data, a written agreement comes first
The tool goes on the approved list, with who may use it and for what data
